scenario: AITA for not wanting to attend my great aunt's funeral? | So today I came home from college (Britain, so American High School, I think). The second I walk through the door my mum tells me that her grandma's sister has died. "Your great aunt Wyn died and the funeral will probably be soon." My first thoughts were 'Who?' and 'Why is she telling me this?' I have actually never heard this name before or met this person besides the one time I found out today I had met her when I was still extremely young and unable to walk for myself. This turned into a slight argument as, for some reason, she wanted me to go this funeral, despite knowing I am a really awkward person at funeral's for people I've met more than once, let along a funeral for someone I've met only once and have no idea who is part of the family. The argument ends with her trying to guilt-trip me by outright just saying "Fine, I'll go on my own." in a really sulky way. Her only arguments for me going were that I'd be going out of 'respect' and support for her, despite that she has never once mentioned this great aunt to me even though she supposedly played a massive hand in raising her as my grandmother, and that it's one of the few times we'll see the much larger branch of the family where it's likely to be a few hundred of us, about 10 of which I have seen more than once but still at most 10 times, maybe not even that. To me, it would feel like gatecrashing the funeral for someone else's family and that, even though I am part of the family, no one would want me there since I do not know nor did I know the person who died. I don't know how much this takes precedence over everything else but it felt like it had to reiterated a lot - I have never met this person besides the one time she met me when I was either 1 or 2 years old and the name has never been mentioned to me before now, at least not to my recollection. So, AITA for not wanting to attend someone who is practically a stranger to me's wedding for the sole reason that she's family?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me not to want to attend my great aunt's funeral. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, I came home from college in Britain, which is like an American high school. My mom told me that my great aunt Wyndy died, and the funeral is probably soon. My initial thoughts were confusion because I didn't know who she was. I've never heard her name before, and the only time I met her was when I was extremely young, maybe 1 or 2 years old. So, I don't have any memories or connection to her. My mom wants me to go to the funeral, but I'm really awkward at funerals, especially for people I don't know well. I've only met this great aunt once, and I don't even remember her. My mom's argument is that I should go out of respect and support for her, but she's never mentioned this great aunt before, even though she supposedly played a big role in raising her. That seems contradictory to me. I also feel like attending the funeral would be like gate-crashing someone else's family event. Even though I'm part of the family, I don't know anyone there except maybe a few people I've seen a few times. It's a large family branch, possibly hundreds of people, but I don't know most of them. I don't think they'd want me there since I don't know the person who died or have any connection to her. I'm also thinking about the precedent this sets. If I go to this funeral just because she's family, does that mean I have to attend every family event, even if I don't know the people involved? That feels like it could be a burden on me, especially since I'm still young and trying to establish my own life. On the other hand, I don't want to upset my mom or make her feel like I'm not respecting her or the family. She's trying to guilt-trip me into going, which makes me feel bad. But I also don't want to attend an event where I don't feel comfortable or connected. I'm also considering cultural and familial expectations. In some cultures, attending funerals of extended family is a significant obligation. But in my experience, our family doesn't seem to have that strong of a tradition, especially since my mom hasn't mentioned this great aunt before. It feels more like a sudden expectation without much prior context. I wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I could send a card or a message instead of attending in person. That way, I'm showing respect without having to go through the discomfort of a funeral for someone I don't know. But I'm not sure if that's acceptable or if my mom would see that as sufficient. Another angle is the emotional impact on me. Funerals can be emotionally draining, especially for someone who's not comfortable in those settings. If I go, I might end up feeling more stressed or anxious, which isn't healthy. On the other hand, not going might lead to tension with my mom or other family members. I'm also thinking about the support aspect. My mom says I should go to support her, but I don't feel like I'm in a position to offer meaningful support. I don't know the person who died, so I can't share memories or comfort her in that way. Maybe there's another way to support her without attending the funeral. In summary, I'm torn between respecting family expectations and my own comfort and emotional well-being. I don't feel a strong obligation to attend because I don't know the person, but I also don't want to create conflict with my mom. I'm considering alternatives to attending, like sending a message, but I'm not sure if that's acceptable. I also don't want to set a precedent where I feel pressured to attend every family event, even if I don't feel connected to them. I think the key points are: 1. Lack of personal connection to the deceased. 2. Discomfort with attending funerals for people I don't know. 3. Potential emotional stress from attending. 4. Desire to avoid family conflict. 5. Considering alternatives to attending in person. Based on these points, I'm leaning towards not attending the funeral, but I'm looking for a respectful way to communicate my feelings to my mom without causing further conflict.
